about: Machine-readable changelog of @origingame/engine (docs/release.md §3). kind: patch (0.x.y, compatible) or minor (0.x.0, has breaks). simulation: changed when a game's world can step differently (the golden replays' hashes moved, scripts/replay-gate.ts), else unchanged; versions before 0.6.1 were not measured and say changed. breaking: what a game may have to edit, each with the fix; find lists the identifiers og upgrade searches the game's sources for, codemod a mechanical rewrite it applies. CHANGELOG.md has the prose.

added.member: og.PointerLock, og.Pointers.movement, PointerInput.movementX/movementY, og.PointerMove.movementX/movementY, InjectedInput pointerLock, mouse_move and pointer_lock actions
added.summary: Mouse-look: og.Pointers.movement is the mouse's relative movement this tick (movementX/Y of pointer 0's events summed, zero next tick); og.PointerLock { wanted, locked } lets a game ask for the pointer lock, which the web shell requests on the next press on the canvas, exits when wanted goes false and reports back from pointerlockchange (absolute positions held while locked). Injected pointer events and og.PointerMove carry movementX/Y (0 when omitted); the command channel's mouse_move:dx,dy and pointer_lock:on|off script them. Native runs are headless and never lock. Off by default; the simulation of existing games is unchanged.

og cook takes .mp3, .ogg (Vorbis) and .flac sounds beside .wav: decoded to 16-bit PCM in the cook (pure Rust, symphonia; no ffmpeg or afconvert) and encoded to QOA like a WAV, chunked and streamed the same way, under the source's asset id (audio/theme.mp3, audio/theme.mp3#chunk3). An undecodable file is refused naming the file and its format. The cook only: the runtime and the wasm are unchanged.

fixed.summary: The built-in look presets and style assets (og_cook look STYLES, BUILTINS) are statics, so og carries each CJK font once instead of twice (about 9.7 MB less per platform).
"What works" says the cited examples/* games live in the GitHub repository, not the installed package, and that the archetypes are installed (og new --archetype).

added.member: og api find / og api show
added.summary: Look the API up one entry at a time: og api find <words> lists the reference entries matching the words (name, module, first sentence, then field and parameter docs), one line each; og api show <name> prints one entry in full (signature, fields with defaults, ranges and units, doc) without its IDL source. Both read the wiki of the installed engine package. og-core §7 and og-game §25 teach them.

added.member: UI style fonts cjk and cjkDisplay
added.summary: A style's fonts block takes cjk and cjkDisplay, Simplified Chinese companions that set a label's Chinese beside the role's Latin face, ahead of the locale's fonts. Every built-in style names one matched to its Latin (templates/styles/cjk: Noto Sans SC, Noto Serif SC, ZCOOL KuaiLe, Fusion Pixel; OFL), cooked in only for a game with a zh string table, rendered at run time.

added.member: UI style tone <part> r g b a
added.summary: The frame art's centre colour (og cook measures it from the atlas when a style does not set it): a button's label ink, and the ground any widget reads through it, are judged against it at 7:1.
og.ui: warns when a control is laid out past the screen's edge with no scroll container to bring it back, naming it and by how much.

fixed: Button labels read on what is drawn: a game's primaryColor over a dark neon or scifi body keeps a light label, and a mid-scale colour (crimson) moves away from its ink as little as it takes. The accent highlight now follows the game's primary and reads 5:1 on its wash. Games on a built-in style look different.
A centred or end-aligned label in a column takes the column's width (it sat at the start in a box as wide as its text).

The neon style: its glow marks the button and the title only (no panel, HUD or number glow; tighter tube halos, a fainter grid), and its numbers are Chakra Petch SemiBold (Orbitron read 0 as Ø and 1 as 7).
AnchorDesc.margin's doc says it insets every edge; no IDL member added or removed.

added.summary: With the variable set (Origin Runner sets it when Origin Desktop draws the Session's engine), og run and og dev show their frames in the desktop window through shared GPU memory and render at the size the window asks for; without it nothing changes.

fixed: level-texturing's texture-level.ts paints with gemini-nano-banana-2.1 by default (qwen-image-2.1-pro stays one --model away); its http provider sends Qwen's seed and prompt_extend only to Qwen models and the view's size to the others, which Gemini's route requires; a resumed run keeps its model.

added: MaterialStyle.shadowDarkness (0 to 1, 0 off): where the sun does not reach (the toon ramp's dark band, the side turned away, a cast shadow) a lit surface loses that share of the sun and of the ambient light, so 1 draws shadows as solid black masses; local lights, emissive and shadowTint still show. RenderCapabilities.stylise names it shadowDarkness.

The cook paints a model's own colour textures with the look's Stylise paint fields in texel space (Kuwahara along the edges, bleed, pigment pooling, canvas grain), as it paints 2D sprites, when the project's look has an art contract that conforms models; textures no model claims, normal and data maps are not painted. Painted 3D textures re-cook and their frames change (painterly-3d, sculpted-clay, paper-craft on their samples).

The cook holds a model that says `conform character` (its type model text, or a glTF's import settings) to ArtShape.characterFaces, as a skinned one, and og style check judges it so; a type model past its face budget is built again with fewer segments before it is decimated.

MaterialStyle.surface (MaterialSurface none, clay, paper, plastic), surfaceStrength and surfaceScale: a made surface on every lit standard material (normal detail, colour grain, wrapped light and roughness in the mesh's own space), none by default; the sculpted-clay, paper-craft and miniature-diorama presets set it and their frames change.
fixed: The heavy-ink-shadows preset draws its shadows as solid black ink (MaterialStyle.shadowDarkness 1; shadowTint at amount 0 had no effect, and posterize never reaches black because the ambient light lifts every shadow), with a near-black sky, a blood-red haze and muted colour. Its frames change.

The low-resolution-3d preset ends its draw distance in a short dark fog the colour of its sky (the clear colour), so the 240-line frame reads as early-console 3D; its vertex snapping and affine texturing were already drawn. Its frames change.

MaterialStyle.surface no longer draws black blots where a mesh's shading normal lies in its face (a smooth silhouette or a rim turning away): the bump fades out there and the normal stays, instead of a NaN the post effects spread. Rumpus Isle's look sets surface none to keep its own colours under miniature-diorama.

The cook's mesh conformance (ArtShape.normals flat) drops faces thinner than the position grid and keeps flat normals on lathe poles and on voxelised parts turned by their placement; conformed models re-cook (model desc conform-mesh-v3).
RenderScene::set_shader_param writes a changed parameter into the material's uniform in place and keeps its bind group, instead of rebuilding both; frames are unchanged.

Stylise.dither and ArtPalette.dither bayer4 and bayer8 use the dispersed Bayer matrix; they drew a quadrant-clustered one whose tones showed as blocks of the matrix's size. Frames and cook-conformed textures dithered with them change; bayer2 does not.
The rubber-hose-animation and gothic-contour presets no longer posterize: per-channel steps turned their sepia and blue-grey art into olive, pink and violet bands. Their frames change.

breaking.change: A project whose look (project.ogt look, or one extending a preset) sets art blocks now cooks its assets conformed to them: 2D art to the pixel grid, the palette and the line (and, with stream A3, models, mesh textures and clips to the shape, texel and motion contract). Frames of such a game change. With stream A4 such a project (one naming its look in project.ogt) also draws under the contract's runtime defaults: cleanEdge pixel-art rotation, the line on sprites the cook did not line, ArtCamera's preset on an applied look, ArtMotion.stepFps as the animation step. At run time, a look with art blocks also sets the camera from ArtCamera when applied, defaults Sprite.outline from ArtLine, draws pixel art through cleanEdge under ArtPixels.rotation cleanEdge, and defaults AnimationPlayer.stepFps from ArtMotion.stepFps, which changes the ticks of a game whose animation drives play (rubber-hose-animation, sculpted-clay).
breaking.fix: Keep it (the style is the point), or opt an asset out with conform off in its import settings or project.ogt conform { off ... }, or set the preset's art blocks to zero in the game's look. At run time: a player whose own AnimationPlayer.stepFps is above 0 keeps it, and ArtMotion { stepFps 0 } in the game's look turns the default off; the camera preset is applied with the look, before GameDesc.start, so camera code in start or later wins.

added.summary: New resource (module art): the palette the assets' texels sit on: colors, strict, maxColors, rampSteps, accents, dither; no constraint at zero.
New resource: the pixel grid of 2D art: unit, logicalHeight, spriteSizes, rotation, rotationSteps, snap; no constraint at zero.
New resource: texel density on 3D surfaces: density, maxSize, filter, mips; no constraint at zero.
New resource: the shape language of models: propFaces, characterFaces, normals, normalAngle, bevel, voxel, silhouette; no constraint at zero.
New resource: the line the assets carry: width, color, place, distanceFalloff; no line at width 0.
New resource: stepFps, maxFrames, squash; no constraint at zero.
New resource: projection, fixedAngle, pitch, yaw, fovMin, fovMax, pixelPerfect; no constraint at zero.
New enum: free, nearest, cleanEdge, prerotated.
New enum: any, nearest, linear.
New enum: any, full, none.
New enum: any, smooth, flat, angle.
New enum: outside, inside, both.
New enum: any, perspective, orthographic.
Left out or empty, project.ogt's look "looks/<id>.ogt" line is applied when it has one; the two naming different looks is refused. A project without the line runs as before.
Names the art resources a look sets too.
Inside a system, an art resource the system does not declare among its writes is left as it is instead of refusing the look.
A look's blocks include the seven art resources, checked against their records as the frame's are; the 37 presets carry their catalogue style's values.
project.ogt's look "looks/<id>.ogt" names the look whose art contract the cook reads before any asset cooks; create writes it beside GameDesc.look.
The brush the cook draws a 2D line with (og.ArtBrush); diamond at zero.
New enum: diamond, circle, square.

The cook conforms sprites, flipbooks, tile sets and UI images to the look's art contract (pixel grid, 1-bit alpha, Oklab palette with dither, line, prerotated cells, painted 2D) and writes <id>#index for palette swaps; conform off and project.ogt conform { off } opt out; og cook --report lists every change. Byte-identical without a contract.

Knowledge (scripts/brief.ts) and @origingame/create-game: artBrief(look, kind, subject, options?) compiles the flattened look and its catalogue entry into the request for one asset: prompt, references, generator parameters; readLook(dir) and presetLook(slug) read a look from disk. A public contract (docs/art.md §2.2).

og style check [project] [--title|--play|--results <commands>] [--size WxH] [--no-frames] [--critic] [--json]: every cooked asset measured against the look's art contract (palette hit rate within ΔE00 2, colours, pixel grid and half pixels, line, texel size, filter and mips, faces against the budget, flat-normal share, texel density and spread), every opt-out listed, and the title, play and results frames (project.ogt's screens block) measured; --critic prints the catalogue's three checks and the frames only. og doctor --project has a style line; og build --publish prints it as warnings, never refusing.

A pixel outline this many logical pixels wide (0 to 4), drawn by the sprite shader from the texture's alpha; 0 is none, or under the project's art contract the look's ArtLine.width for a texture the cook did not line.
The outline's linear colour; at its default, the art contract's ArtLine.color.
A palette swap: the sprite draws its texture's index texture (the cook's <id>#index) through a row of this palette texture of N rows; 0 is none.
The row of Sprite.palette drawn.
A palette swap of every tile layer through a row of this palette texture; 0 is none.
The row of Tilemap.palette drawn.

Under project.ogt's look (stream A4): ArtPixels.rotation cleanEdge draws pixel-art textures through the new cleanEdge sampler (og-render TextureFilter::CleanEdge), ArtLine defaults Sprite.outline, ArtCamera sets the camera's projection, angle and field of view when a look is applied and pixelPerfect snaps the 2D camera by logical pixels, ArtMotion.stepFps defaults AnimationPlayer.stepFps, and a strict ArtPalette tints the UI's icons to their nearest palette colour. Without the look line nothing changes.

added: Knowledge: the craft skills architecture-discipline, component-forge, level-texturing (with scripts/texture-level.ts), localization, recipe-craft and visual-acceptance move from origin-agent into the knowledge package under the same names, free of platform tools and pointing to the og-* skills and the wiki for the API; texture-level.ts's providers are handoff (default), http (an OpenAI-compatible image endpoint) and dashscope, and runs that say agent or gateway resume.

Knowledge: payload(roots) and defaultRoots(pkg?) of knowledge/scripts/lib.ts, with the PayloadFile and Roots shapes, are a public contract beside installed, mount and summary: the platform reads the knowledge straight from the installed package with payload(installed(dir).roots). Nothing about them changed.

fixed: og check on a TypeScript install that bun x left incomplete (tsgo, where tsrs has no package): instead of tsgo's Go panic or Cannot find global type errors, it names the incomplete directory and the fix (delete it or bun pm cache rm, then rerun); og doctor reports it as broken.

The knowledge package's scripts/mount.ts CLI mounts into an origin-agent checkout's knowledge/, where the platform's knowledge moved from OriginGame's packages/game-knowledge/production; installed, mount and summary are unchanged.

og-ui glass on WebGL2 in Chrome and Edge on Windows blurs as on metal, WebGPU and DX12: each pyramid level took its tap spacing from textureDimensions of a view whose base mip level is that level, which ANGLE on D3D11 answers with level 2b's size for base level b, so the blur was about twice as wide. Each level of the glass pyramid and of a view's glow chain now takes the size it reads from a uniform; native frames are unchanged.

WebGL2 starts about four times faster on Windows (ANGLE on D3D11): programs link in the background with KHR_parallel_shader_compile, read when a pass first draws with them, and the GL tier's lit programs leave the rect-light (LTC) code out until a scene has a rect light. fx-showcase's cold first frame went from 30.4-31.7 s to 7.0-7.5 s in Chrome 155 and from 30.3-31.2 s to 7.6-7.7 s in Edge 155; WebGPU, metal and DX12 are unchanged and no frame moved. The trade-off: on WebGL2, a scene that gets its first rect light during play links its lit programs again at that moment (about 5 to 8 s on ANGLE D3D11, waited for by the next lit frame); to pay it at load instead, put an og.RectLight in the first scene (one at intensity 0 counts).

added.summary: og bake projection init|plan|prepare|project|holes|export --run <dir>: a gray level glb painted from planned views by an image model the caller runs, projected into one texture and exported as a textured glb, on the CPU.

fixed: A NavAgent with faceMovement turns the same on every host: its turn was glam's slerp on the host's sinf and drifted by up to 16 ulp between Windows and Linux for the ticks of a turn; it is now a yaw step through og-core's deterministic math, so the turning ticks' quaternions move by an ulp on every host.
og.terrain.sample's slope is computed with og-core's deterministic acos instead of the host's.

camera.worldToScreen and camera.screenToRay, which a system may call inside the tick, answer the same bits on every host: their perspective is built with og-core's sin/cos (not glam's host-libm perspective), now pinned by a test, and glam's perspective constructors are refused in the simulation crates.

added.summary: og upgrade [project] [--to <v>] [--json]: moves project.ogt's engine pin and package.json's dependency, applies the codemods of the versions crossed and lists what needs a hand edit; exit 0 done, 3 manual edits, 1 failed.

og replay record and og replay compare: a game's per-tick world hashes recorded with one engine version and replayed with another; the first divergent tick and the entities, components and fields that differ.
og doctor --json: the checks as one object, with pin { pinned, installed, compatible }.
This file, in the package: each version's kind, whether the simulation changed, its breaks with their fixes, additions and fixes.
Zoom, spin and directional blurs of the frame with screenBlurStrength, screenBlurCenter, screenBlurAngle and screenBlurSamples; off at none or strength 0.
Resource that sways og.TerrainScatter copies (strength, direction, speed, gust); visual only, off at strength 0.
How much og.Wind sways a scatter: 1 as it blows, 0 still.
Barrel or pincushion distortion with lensDistortionCenter; off at 0.
Variant neutral (Khronos PBR Neutral), appended; existing indices unchanged.

Colour adjustments after the LUT: temperature, tint, brightness, contrast, balanceShadows, balanceMidtones, balanceHighlights, preserveLuminosity, hue, saturation, vibrance, grayscale, invert, threshold; each off at 0.

fixed: WebGL2 starts on Windows in Chrome and Edge (ANGLE on D3D11).
The 2D publish build's refusal of a 3D world names its scenes with / on Windows.
A debug og-gfx no longer overflows Windows' 1 MiB main-thread stack.
